nodes.name: 200 OK
nodes.notes: Answer Bitrix immediately. A webhook sender must never wait on a model call.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO raw_events (source, external_ref, payload, payload_hash)
VALUES ('bitrix_webhook', $1, $2::jsonb, encode(digest($2::text, 'sha256'), 'hex'))
ON CONFLICT (source, payload_hash) DO NOTHING
RETURNING raw_id;

nodes.name: Land raw (idempotent)
nodes.notes:
Query params are an ARRAY expression, not a comma-separated string. The payload is JSON and full of commas — a comma-separated list would be split into dozens of bogus parameters.

ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING means a redelivered webhook returns zero rows and the branch below stops. Replay always starts from here, never from Bitrix.

nodes.name: Parse & compute metrics
nodes.notes:
Private-network URL: no public internet, no egress billing.

Auth is an n8n Header Auth credential (X-API-Key) rather than $env, so the secret never sits in this JSON and n8n's env-access setting is irrelevant.

Normalisation, phone E.164 and every computed metric happen in Python. n8n never does arithmetic that ends up in a score.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO interactions (
  external_source, external_id, channel, started_at, ended_at,
  customer_phone_raw, customer_phone_e164, is_bot_handled, handled_by,
  message_count, customer_message_count, agent_message_count,
  first_response_seconds, is_after_hours
) VALUES (
  'bitrix', $1, $2::channel, $3::timestamptz, $4::timestamptz,
  $5, $6, $7::boolean,
  CASE WHEN $7::boolean THEN 'bot'::speaker_role ELSE 'agent'::speaker_role END,
  $8::int, $9::int, $10::int, $11::int, $12::boolean
)
ON CONFLICT (external_source, external_id) DO UPDATE SET
  ended_at               = EXCLUDED.ended_at,
  message_count          = EXCLUDED.message_count,
  customer_message_count = EXCLUDED.customer_message_count,
  agent_message_count    = EXCLUDED.agent_message_count,
  first_response_seconds = EXCLUDED.first_response_seconds,
  is_bot_handled         = EXCLUDED.is_bot_handled,
  updated_at             = now()
RETURNING interaction_id;

INSERT INTO chat_messages (interaction_id, seq, sender, body, sent_at)
SELECT $1::uuid,
       (m->>'seq')::int,
       (m->>'sender')::speaker_role,
       m->>'body',
       (m->>'sent_at')::timestamptz
FROM jsonb_array_elements($2::jsonb) AS m
ON CONFLICT (interaction_id, sender, sent_at, body_hash) DO NOTHING;

nodes.name: Insert messages (dedup)
nodes.notes:
The webhook resends the WHOLE thread every time. The unique key on (interaction_id, sender, sent_at, body_hash) is what stops five webhooks becoming five copies of every message.

The message array is passed as ONE jsonb parameter and expanded in SQL, so Arabic text containing commas cannot corrupt the parameter list.

nodes.name: Human agent involved?
nodes.notes: Bot-only threads stop here. Grading a human on the qualification bot's messages makes every QA number wrong.

nodes.name: Wait for thread to settle
nodes.notes:
A conversation grows over days. Re-running the judge on every webhook is expensive and produces churn; this waits until the thread has been idle before spending a model call.

TESTING: set this to 1 minute for the first end-to-end run, then put it back to 30. A Wait longer than ~65s only resumes reliably when the workflow is PUBLISHED, not in a manual execution.

parameters.query:
SELECT count(*)::int AS newer
FROM chat_messages
WHERE interaction_id = $1::uuid
  AND sent_at > $2::timestamptz;

nodes.name: Newer messages arrived?
nodes.notes: If the thread grew while we waited, a later run will evaluate the fuller version. Abandoning this run avoids paying twice and avoids a stale score overwriting a fresh one.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ conversation: $('Parse & compute metrics').item.json.transcript_text, input_type: 'chat', metadata: $('Parse & compute metrics').item.json.metrics, run_pass1: true, run_pass2: true }) }}

nodes.name: Two AI passes
nodes.notes: One HTTP call, two separate DeepSeek requests inside. Pass 1 (customer) and pass 2 (agent) never see each other's output, so an angry customer cannot drag down the agent's score.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO interaction_analysis (
  interaction_id, schema_version, prompt_version, model, input_type,
  language, intent, summary_ar, confidence, uncertain_fields, raw_response
) VALUES (
  $1::uuid, '1.0', $2, $3, 'chat'::input_type,
  $4, $5, $6, $7::numeric, $8::jsonb, $9::jsonb
)
ON CONFLICT (interaction_id) DO UPDATE SET
  summary_ar   = EXCLUDED.summary_ar,
  confidence   = EXCLUDED.confidence,
  raw_response = EXCLUDED.raw_response,
  updated_at   = now();

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $('Upsert interaction').item.json.interaction_id, $json.pass1.prompt_version, $json.pass1.model, ($json.pass1.payload.language || null), ($json.pass1.payload.intent || null), ($json.pass1.payload.summary_ar || null), ($json.pass1.payload.confidence ?? null), JSON.stringify($json.pass1.payload.uncertain_fields || []), JSON.stringify($json.pass1.payload) ] }}

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO agent_evaluations (
  interaction_id, schema_version, prompt_version, rubric_version, model,
  input_type, final_score, performance_level, weight_applied,
  m1_reception, m2_offer, m3_objections, m4_followup, m5_closing,
  breakdown, evidence, stage_reached, behavior_flags,
  top_strength, top_weakness, top_recommendation, notes, raw_response
) VALUES (
  $1::uuid, '1.0', $2, $3, $4, 'chat'::input_type,
  $5::numeric, $6, $7::numeric,
  $8::numeric, $9::numeric, $10::numeric, $11::numeric, $12::numeric,
  $13::jsonb, $14::jsonb, $15::conversation_stage, $16::jsonb,
  $17, $18, $19, $20, $21::jsonb
)
ON CONFLICT (interaction_id) DO UPDATE SET
  final_score       = EXCLUDED.final_score,
  performance_level = EXCLUDED.performance_level,
  weight_applied    = EXCLUDED.weight_applied,
  m1_reception      = EXCLUDED.m1_reception,
  m2_offer          = EXCLUDED.m2_offer,
  m3_objections     = EXCLUDED.m3_objections,
  m4_followup       = EXCLUDED.m4_followup,
  m5_closing        = EXCLUDED.m5_closing,
  breakdown         = EXCLUDED.breakdown,
  evidence          = EXCLUDED.evidence,
  raw_response      = EXCLUDED.raw_response,
  updated_at        = now();

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $('Upsert interaction').item.json.interaction_id, $json.pass2.prompt_version, $json.rubric_version, $json.pass2.model, $json.pass2.final_score, $json.pass2.performance_level, $json.pass2.weight_applied, $json.pass2.modules.module1_reception, $json.pass2.modules.module2_offer, $json.pass2.modules.module3_objections, $json.pass2.modules.module4_followup, $json.pass2.modules.module5_closing, JSON.stringify($json.pass2.payload.modules), JSON.stringify($json.pass2.payload.evidence || []), ($json.pass2.payload.stage_reached || null), JSON.stringify($json.pass2.payload.behavior_flags || []), ($json.pass2.payload.summary?.top_strength || null), ($json.pass2.payload.summary?.top_weakness || null), ($json.pass2.payload.summary?.top_recommendation || null), ($json.pass2.payload.notes || null), JSON.stringify($json.pass2.payload) ] }}

nodes.name: Store evaluation
nodes.notes: Module scores may be null — that means the situation never arose, which is different from zero. The column is nullable on purpose and weight_applied records the denominator actually used.
